papers.title: Canonical Volumes of Threefolds with Positive Geometric Genus
papers.summary: We prove that a complex projective threefold of general type with canonical singularities and positive geometric genus has canonical volume at least $1/30$, with strict inequality when its Euler characteristic is positive. We describe the equality cases as canonical hypersurfaces of degree $28$ in $\mathbb P(1,3,4,5,14)$. These canonical models and their smooth projective resolutions are simply connected. Their coarse moduli space is irreducible and rational of dimension $103$, with finite quotient singularities; all admissible $\mathbb Q$-Gorenstein deformations are unobstructed and arise by varying the equation.

papers.title: K3 tails in the KSBA moduli of Kunev surfaces
papers.summary: In the context of compact moduli spaces of Kollár, Shepherd-Barron, and Alexeev stable surfaces, a degeneration can acquire an exceptional K3 component in the limit, or more simply a K3 tail. We study this phenomenon for Kunev surfaces: minimal surfaces of general type with $K^2=p_g=1$ that arise as $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2$-covers of the projective plane branched along two general cubics and a line. We classify the K3 tails that occur when the branch curve degenerates to a singular curve with a non-log canonical isolated semi-quasihomogeneous singularity, and describe the corresponding boundary strata. This builds on the Kerr-Laza classification of K3 tails arising from isolated semi-quasihomogeneous hypersurface singularities.

papers.title: Permutation polynomials of given index up to quasi-multiplicative equivalence
papers.summary: Let $q$ be a prime power and let $\ell$ be a divisor of $q-1$. We classify the permutation polynomials of $\mathbb F_q$ of polynomial index exactly $\ell$ up to quasi-multiplicative equivalence $G(X)\equiv uF(vX^d)\pmod{X^q-X}$, where $u,v\in\mathbb F_q^*$ and $\gcd(d,q-1)=1$, and we count the classes. For polynomials vanishing at $0$, the classes are the orbits of an explicit finite group on vectors of values at the $\ell$-th roots of unity. Through the permutation it induces on the roots of unity, each orbit lies over a double coset of the symmetric group $S_\ell$ with respect to its translation subgroup and an explicit affine group, and the stabilizers are explicit. For polynomials with nonzero constant term the action is free. Burnside's lemma, Möbius inversion over the coefficient support and congruences along the cycles of affine permutations give an exact formula for the number of classes. For fixed $\ell\geqslant2$ these numbers are quasi-polynomials in $s=(q-1)/\ell$ of degree at most $\ell-1$, with period dividing $\ell$ for odd $\ell$ and $2\ell$ for even $\ell$; for polynomials vanishing at $0$ the degree is exactly $\ell-1$, and we determine the leading coefficient. For odd prime $\ell$ and for $\ell=4$ the counts are given in closed form. For index four we also count the binomials and trinomials at each admissible coefficient support. The sums of two binomial counts that occur are expressed through quartic Jacobi sums and Frobenius traces of elliptic curves and of a curve of genus two; one of the elliptic curves is the reduction of the curve $Y^2=X^3+8X^2+32X$, which has no complex multiplication over $\mathbb Q$. The trinomial counts are expressed through quartic cyclotomic numbers and these sums. All these terms cancel when the counts with a fixed residue of the vanishing order modulo $s$ are added.

papers.title: Equidistribution of curves in hypersurfaces of low degree
papers.summary: We prove that over $\mathbb{C}$, for any smooth projective curve $\mathscr{C}$ and any smooth hypersurface $V \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ of degree $d$ such that $n \geq 2^d(d-1)$, Faisant's equidistribution principle holds for $(\mathscr{C},V)$. In other words, for any reasonable set of jet conditions $W$, the moduli space $\mathrm{Hom}^e(\mathscr{C},V|W)$ of degree $e$ maps $\mathscr{C} \to V$ satisfying conditions $W$ converges in the Grothendieck ring of complex varieties, after renormalisation, as $e \to \infty$. This provides the dimension and decomposition into irreducible components of $\mathrm{Hom}^e(\mathscr{C},V|W)$ for $e$ large enough. The strategy follows Bilu and Browning's motivic version of the circle method, and Hase-Liu's framework for genus $\geq 1$.

papers.title: Specializations of frozen variables for Grassmannian cluster algebra
papers.summary: The homogeneous coordinate ring of a Grassmannian variety $\mathrm{Gr}_{k,n}$ is equipped with a structure of a cluster algebra. The frozen variables are identified with the Plücker coordinates corresponding to length-$k$ segments of ${\mathbb Z}_n$. We study two families of algebras: the first family is obtained by specializing all the frozen variables and the second corresponds to the specialization of the nonwrapping variables. We construct flat bases in both families and study their affine spectra. The special fibers of the families are cones over projective varieties. We identify the irreducible components of these projective varieties with certain positroid varieties.

papers.title: Combinatorics of noncommutative harmonic oscillator determinant
papers.summary: We obtain an explicit evaluation of the determinants that appear in the denominators of the integrands for the iterated integrals expressing special values of the spectral zeta function of the noncommutative harmonic oscillator at integers greater than 1. The determinants in question are those of cyclic tridiagonal matrices; their explicit evaluation is carried out, in addition to the inclusion-exclusion principle, conceptionally using combinatorial arguments based on monomer-dimer systems. This explicit evaluation serves as a core component in the study of arithmetic properties such as the modularity of the special values of the spectral zeta function.

papers.title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties
papers.summary: Building on Liu's and Liu--Sheshmani's systematized description of Kontsevich's localization methods in toric varieties, we develop a computational framework for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of smooth projective toric varieties and their smooth complete intersections. This is grounded in equivariant localization and the combinatorial structure of toric fans. We describe how the geometric data required by the localization formulas can be recovered directly from the fan and extend the existing software for flag varieties to compute the small quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. The implementation also incorporates cyclic determinants and regularized-exponent multisets, providing computational tools for investigating the atomic decomposition of quantum cohomology. Using this framework, we obtain the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^5$. Also applying new methods to study Hodge atoms in Fano fivefolds, we recover the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^7$, due to Cavenaghi--Katzarkov--Kontsevich, and we prove the nonrationality of every smooth quartic double fivefold and every smooth quartic fivefold.

papers.fulltext_excerpt: [2611.16068] On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties Skip to main content Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search --> Mathematics > Algebraic Geometry arXiv:2611.16068 (math) [Submitted on 11 Nov 2026] Title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties Authors: Milena Brockhof , Giovane Galindo , Ludmil Katzarkov , Pedro Antonio Muniz Martins View a PDF of the paper titled On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties, by Milena Brockhof and 3 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Building on Liu's and Liu--Sheshmani's systematized description of Kontsevich's localization methods in toric varieties, we develop a computational framework for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of smooth projective toric varieties and their smooth complete intersections. This is grounded in equivariant localization and the combinatorial structure of toric fans. We describe how the geometric data required by the localization formulas can be recovered directly from the fan and extend the existing software for flag varieties to compute the small quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. The implementation also incorporates cyclic determinants and regularized-exponent multisets, providing computational tools for investigating the atomic decomposition of quantum cohomology. Using this framework, we obtain the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^5$. Also applying new methods to study Hodge atoms in Fano fivefolds, we recover the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^7$, due to Cavenaghi--Katzarkov--Kontsevich, and we prove the nonrationality of every smooth quartic double fivefold and every smooth quartic fivefold. papers.title: Perfect loops of proper schemes
papers.summary: We study the perfect loop space $LX$ of a proper scheme $X$ over a local field $F$. We show that if $X$ contains a rational curve, then $LX$ is not ind-representable, even in a very weak sense. We also show that if $X$ admits a proper model $\mathfrak{X}$ over the integers $\mathcal{O}$ of $F$, whose geometric special fiber does not contain rational curves, then $L^+\mathfrak{X} \stackrel{\sim}{\to} LX$ is an isomorphism via the natural map, where $L^+\mathfrak{X}$ denotes the perfect positive loop space (jet scheme) of $\mathfrak{X}$. In particular, $LX$ is a scheme in this case.

papers.title: Independence of Hasse--Weil $L$-functions over rings of Dirichlet series
papers.summary: We study linear and algebraic independence of Hasse--Weil $L$-functions of abelian varieties over $\mathbb{Q}$, with Dirichlet series as coefficients. For nonzero varieties that are pairwise non-isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, we prove that their $L$-functions with arbitrary Dirichlet twists, together with all their derivatives and $1$, are linearly independent when the coefficient series use only primes from a set of natural density zero. For untwisted $L$-functions, this independence is equivalent to the condition that the varieties are pairwise non-isogenous over $\mathbb{Q}$. If the individual monodromy groups are connected, the result for varieties that are pairwise non-isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ extends to larger coefficient rings: the prime supports of coefficients are unrestricted outside a prescribed set of positive upper natural density and meet it in a set of natural density zero. We also characterize algebraic independence of untwisted $L$-functions in terms of the multiplicities of the simple isogeny factors of the varieties. The proofs combine an arithmetic-function lemma of Kaczorowski--Molteni--Perelli with Frobenius density arguments and require no analytic continuation or automorphy.

papers.title: Extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces without Gaussian maps and classification of prime Fano threefolds
authors: with an appendix written jointly with Anand Deopurkar
papers.summary: In arXiv:2409.03960 an approach to the question of extendability of projective varieties via degeneration to ribbons was introduced, and in arXiv:2503.12661 it was used to give a new proof of optimal results on the extendability of general non-prime $K3$ surfaces and the classification of non-prime Fano threefolds. In this article we treat the prime case. We give a new proof of the optimal results on the extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces of every genus, of the classification of prime Fano threefolds of Picard rank one due to Fano, Iskovskikh and Mukai, and of the irreducibility of their Hilbert schemes. This involves degenerations of $K3$ surfaces to ribbons on embedded rational normal scrolls, called $K3$ carpets. We compute exactly the cohomology of the twisted normal bundle of these $K3$ carpets, instead of computing coranks of Gaussian maps of the canonical curve sections. The key challenge is to analyze the coboundary map of the sequence relating the normal bundle of the $K3$ carpet to the normal bundle of the scroll. We give a deformation theoretic interpretation of this map. Given such a $K3$ carpet and its hyperplane section, which is a canonical ribbon, we show that the coboundary map corresponds to the obstruction to lifting a first order deformation of the underlying scroll fixing the underlying rational normal curve to a first order deformation of the $K3$ carpet fixing the canonical ribbon. To compute the obstruction, we use a result on extensions of non-split ribbons on any curve to a unique $K$-trivial carpet in a canonical way.

papers.title: A Lefschetz Alternative for Real Characters on Smooth Quasi-Projective Varieties
papers.summary: We establish a Lefschetz alternative for real characters on smooth complex quasi-projective varieties, extending Simpson's classical theorem beyond the compact Kähler setting. More precisely, for a nonzero real character of the fundamental group of a smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety, either the character factors through a holomorphic fibration onto a Riemann orbifold with connected general fiber, or every level set of an associated primitive function on the corresponding covering is connected and its inclusion induces a surjection onto the fundamental group of the covering. Our approach combines logarithmic holomorphic $1$-forms with a geometric flow construction to overcome the difficulties arising from noncompactness. Meanwhile, we prove a quasi-projective analogue of the Napier--Ramachandran theorem, showing that an epimorphism onto $\Z $ whose kernel is not finitely generated must factor through a hyperbolic Riemann orbifold. As applications, we derive several new restrictions on the structure of quasi-projective groups.

papers.title: Critical schemes, jet syzygies, and twisted periods
papers.summary: We study nonreduced critical schemes with prescribed support on nilpotent orbit closures and on the Kleinian singularity $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, and show that one specified minimal invariant syzygy among the first jet equations fixes their scheme structure. For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_N$ or $\mathfrak{so}_{2N}$ with Coxeter number $h$ and $p\ge2$ coprime to $h$, the selected polynomial is the coefficient of $s^{p+1}$ in $\det(1-sM)^{p/h}$, with reduced critical locus $\{M^p=0\}$, and the selecting syzygy is equivalent to the twisted period equation of Dubrovin and Feigin-Silantyev. The minimal invariant syzygies of that degree correspond to the lowest nonquadratic twisted periods, which, for $\mathfrak{so}_8$, form the standard representation of triality; in type D the Betti number alone does not determine the scheme. On $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, the selected polynomial is given by a terminating hypergeometric series. Restriction to Slodowy slices commutes with forming critical schemes and their nilradicals. These results determine, uniformly in rank and degree, the rings and nilradical filtrations through which the Schur and Macdonald indices of the corresponding Argyres-Douglas theories are proposed to arise as Hilbert series of arc spaces.

papers.title: Complex singularities and obstructions to pseudo-Einstein structures: An expository note
papers.summary: This note explains the counterexamples to Lee's conjecture on pseudo-Einstein structures obtained in joint work with Yoshinori Gongyo, Kengo Hirachi, and Shuya Matsumoto. The examples are links of normal isolated singularities and occur in every odd real dimension at least three. Each link has vanishing first Betti number and vanishing integral first Chern class of its CR structure, yet admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. We explain how finite first homology relates the existence problem on the link to the canonical divisor at the singular point. For the higher-dimensional examples, we describe the key obstruction directly in terms of the first normal derivatives of the transition functions of a line bundle along an exceptional hypersurface.

papers.title: Differential properties of Drinfeld modular forms
papers.summary: We study the action of vector fields on the Drinfeld symmetric spaces on de Rham classes of the generic Drinfeld module. The resulting Kodaira-Spencer map is an isomorphism, and is described by the Jacobian matrix \(J := (\frac{\partial g_{j}}{\partial ω_{i}})_{1 \leq i,j \leq r}\), where the \(g_{j}\) are the basic coefficient modular forms of rank \(r\). We show that \(J\) is the matrix inverse of the period matrix \(P\) that results from the de Rham theory of Drinfeld modules. We define the notion of Drinfeld modular differential form, which generalizes the transformation behavior of Drinfeld modular forms from functions to differential \(n\)-forms on the Drinfeld symmetric space \(Ω^{r}\). The algebra \(\mathbf{M}^{(*)} = \bigoplus_{0 \leq n < r} \mathbf{M}^{(n)}\) of all such is provided with a Serre derivation \(D \colon \mathbf{M}^{(n)} \to \mathbf{M}^{(n+1)}\) from \(n\)-forms to \((n+1)\)-forms, where \(\mathbf{M}^{(0)} = \mathbf{M}\) is the algebra of customary modular forms for \(\mathrm{GL}(r, \mathbb{F}_{q}[T])\). We determine the structure of \(\mathbf{M}^{(*)}\), which turns out to be the exterior algebra \(\bigwedge (\mathbf{M}^{(1)})\) of the \(\mathbf{M}\)-module \(\mathbf{M}^{(1)}\).

papers.title: Unramified case of Colliot-Thélène conjecture on quadratic forms
papers.summary: The Colliot-Thélène conjecture on quadratic forms asserts that any rationally isotropic nondegenerate quadratic form over a semilocal regular domain with $2$ invertible is isotropic. We prove the Colliot-Thélène conjecture for semilocal regular domains that are geometrically regular over a discrete valuation ring with $2$ invertible. In particular, this includes unramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, where $p\neq 2$.

papers.title: Exotic smooth structures on complex projective spaces
papers.summary: We study smooth structures on the topological manifold underlying complex projective space. We conjecture that every complex projective space $\mathbb{CP}^n$ with $n>3$ admits an exotic smooth structure. We prove two results providing strong evidence for this conjecture. First, the set of complex dimensions $n$ for which $\mathbb{CP}^n$ admits an exotic smooth structure has natural density one. Second, we explicitly identify $266$ congruence classes modulo $288$ such that $\mathbb{CP}^n$ admits an exotic smooth structure whenever $n>3$ lies in one of these classes. These classes cover more than $92\%$ of complex dimensions, improving the previously known lower bound of approximately $36\%$. We prove these results by first relating the concordance group of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ to suitable Atiyah--Hirzebruch filtration subgroups of its stable cohomotopy group, and then applying computations in chromatic homotopy theory at height $2$.

papers.title: Finiteness of strongly reflective modular forms
papers.summary: Let $Γ\subset\mathrm{O}^+(n,2)$ be a rational arithmetic group with $n\geq 3$. A non-constant modular form for $Γ$ is called strongly reflective if its zero divisor is a reduced union of mirrors of reflections in $Γ$. We show that, up to conjugation and multiplication by a nonzero scalar, there are only finitely many strongly reflective modular forms. As a consequence, we establish the finiteness of holomorphic automorphic products of singular weight. These results answer a question posed by Borcherds in 1995 and settle a conjecture of Gritsenko--Nikulin from 1998. As an application, up to conjugation, we prove the finiteness of $Γ$ whose corresponding algebra of modular forms is freely generated. papers.title: $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded norms for de Rham-Witt forms
papers.summary: We make two case studies of $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded homotopy in connection with $p$-adic cohomology. First, we identify the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf T)$-graded $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings as multi-Rees algebras for the Nygaard and $φ^\bullet(I)$-adic filtrations. papers.summary: For a bounded coherent complex of graded modules over the Raynaud ring $R$, we compare three descriptions of finite torsion: Ekedahl's pieces $A_f^2$ and $A_{\SSpart}^1$ of the biduality filtration, the nilpotent and semisimple parts of the torsion of the Illusie--Raynaud cœur, and the corresponding parts of the finite torsion $t^1$ of Ekedahl's diagonal cohomology. papers.title: Optimal Sample Complexity for Genus-Two Zeta Functions from Noisy Random Euler Products
papers.summary: We study exact recovery of the Hasse--Weil zeta numerator from repeated noisy observations of a randomized Euler product. For a genus-two curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$, we attach independent symmetric signs to its closed points and observe the logarithm of the resulting product at $t_q=c/\sqrt q$, where $0<c<1/\sqrt{12}$ is fixed. For every fixed, known additive noise density $f$ satisfying $\sqrt{f}\in H^1(\mathbb{R})$, we prove that the minimax number of independent observations required for exact recovery with error probability at most $δ$ has order $q^4\log(1/δ)$. No moment condition is imposed on the noise, so the result includes Cauchy readout. The upper bound estimates the phase of an empirical characteristic function and uses the separation of the integral Weil coefficients. The matching lower bound compares the full observation laws for two actual curves with ordinary, absolutely simple Jacobians. It combines a binomial comparison with a uniform bound on the closed-point tail. Thus access to the full observations does not improve the sample order attained by the phase estimator. The result concerns the information in a specified observation channel. It does not assume an efficient implementation of that channel.

papers.title: Nontrivial Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function and Its Derivative
papers.summary: The nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie at the heart of analytic number theory. Through the explicit formulas, they govern the distribution of prime numbers: the closer all nontrivial zeros lie to the critical line $\Re(s)=\frac12$, the more uniformly the primes are distributed. The Riemann Hypothesis-asserting that all nontrivial zeros satisfy $\Re(s)=\frac12$-is equivalent to the optimal error bound $O(\sqrt{x}\log x)$ in the Prime Number Theorem. Beyond number theory, the zeros of $ζ(s)$ and its derivative $ζ'(s)$ are deeply intertwined: the horizontal distribution of $ζ'$-zeros near the critical line encodes information about the spacing of consecutive $ζ$-zeros. This paper establishes some results concerning the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

papers.title: A rank-zero $2$-converse to the Gross--Zagier and Kolyvagin theorem for elliptic curves with abelian two-division field
papers.summary: Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ be an elliptic curve with abelian two-division field. We prove that finiteness of ${\mathrm Sel}_{2^\infty}(E/\mathbb{Q})$ implies $L(E,1)\ne0$. Together with Kato's cyclotomic divisibility and the fixed lattice in his construction, it bounds the denominator by a fixed power of $2$, independently of the twisting primes and the family dimension. Congruences among coefficients of a half-integral-weight form, in the style of Ono--Skinner, construct the required twist families.

papers.title: Newforms as test vectors for representations of Saito-Kurokawa type
papers.summary: We study irreducible (admissible) representations $π$ of the split group $G_n=SO(2n+1)$, both over finite and $p$-adic fields, which are distinguished for the (unramified) nonsplit form of $K_n=SO(2n)$ and for one more subgroup $H_n$. Over finite fields, $H_n$ is the split $SO(2n)$ while over $p$-adic fields it is the Gross-Tsai paramodular subgroup (of minimal level for $π$). These are all multiplicity one situations. With $0 \neq \ell_{n,K} \in {\rm Hom}_{K_n}(π_n,1)$ and $0 \neq v_{n,H} \in π_n^{H_n}$, both being one dimensional spaces, we are interested in the vanishing/nonvanishing of $|\ell_{n,K}(v_{n,H})|^2$. Appropriately normalized, this defines the notion of the correlation coefficient $c(π;H_n,K_n)$ of $H_n$ and $K_n$ in $G_n$ with respect to $π$. Via the theta correspondence between ${\rm SL}(2)$ (or ${\rm Mp}(2)$), we establish a bijection $π_n \leftrightarrow π_1$ between representations of $G_n$ and $G_1$ under consideration. Our main results then prove that $d_n c(π_n;H_n,K_n)$ is independent of the rank $n$, where $d_n =\dim π_n$ for finite fields and is defined in terms of the index of $H_n$ in the standard maximal compact subgroup of $G_n$ in the $p$-adic case. We also highlight a conjecture from [Ana25] on Legendre polynomials modulo $p$. Its truth will have the arithmetic consequence that over $\mathbb F_p$, given $π_1$, we can choose $u \in \mathbb F_p$ such that, in every rank $n$, all the correlation coefficients $c(π_n;H_n,u_nK_n u_n^{-1})$ are simultaneously nonzero and moreover they belong to $\mathbb Z_p^\times$ under any identification $\mathbb C \simeq \overline{\mathbb Q}_p$, where $u_n$ is a specific unipotent element in $G_n$ corresponding to $u$.

papers.title: Counting Rational Points on Cayley's Cubic Surface
papers.summary: We study rational points of bounded maximum-coordinate height on the split four-nodal Cayley cubic surface over \(\mathbb Q\), with its nine lines removed. Writing \(U\) for this open subset and \(N_U(B)\) for its counting function, we establish \[ N_U(B)\sim c_{\mathrm{Peyre}}B(\log B)^6. \] The argument starts from the universal-torsor parametrization and combines two counting methods over complementary ranges of the auxiliary variables. The two-dimensional lattice count is controlled by averages of reciprocal shortest-vector lengths and character-moment bounds, while Poisson summation treats the complementary parameter range. The main contribution is the uniform control needed to combine these methods when the size parameters of the auxiliary variables vary independently: the estimates retain every coprimality condition, the original height weight, and the full set of auxiliary tuples contributing to the geometric error. Divisibility estimates without an additional power of the height parameter control the sieve tail and justify removing the sieve after taking the height limit. We track the derivative losses and boundary contributions throughout the summation, and identify the common continuous main term with Peyre's constant by computing the effective-cone volume and the real and finite local densities.

papers.title: Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations
papers.summary: Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. Zhang for $f$ of higher even weights; and by Yuan--Zhang--Zhang for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form of parallel weight $2$ over an arbitrary totally real field $F$ and $χ$ a Dirichlet character of an arbitrary CM extension $E/F$, allowing arbitrary ramification. papers.title: On Sufficient Conditions for Rank Zero in Families of Elliptic Curves
papers.summary: In this article, we study the Mordell Weil ranks of elliptic curves in the family $E_D:y^2=x^3+Dx$, where $D\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. Under suitable congruence conditions on $D$ and its prime divisors, we use $2$-descent via a rational $2$-isogeny to study the rank of $E_D$. Under our congruence hypotheses, the ranks of these matrices give sufficient conditions for $E_D$ to have rank zero. We give explicit sufficient conditions for the curves $E_D$ to have Mordell Weil rank zero over $\mathbb{Q}$ in the following cases: (i) $D$ is an odd negative integer, (ii) $D$ is an odd positive integer, and (iii) $D$ is a positive even integer. Also we give a quantitative result describing how many square free parameters satisfy the required matrix-rank condition. In particular, our results show that these rank zero criteria hold for a significant proportion of the admissible parameters.

papers.title: Hessenberg character
papers.summary: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group with Borel subgroup $B$, flag variety $\mathcal B=G/B$, and Weyl group $W$. We define the \emph{Hessenberg functor} on the geometric Hecke category by microlocalizing along the diagonal in $\mathcal B\times\mathcal B$ and pushing forward along the Springer map. It induces the \emph{Hessenberg character} of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra, with values in graded $W$-representations. On Kazhdan--Lusztig basis elements indexed by smooth elements of $W$, this character recovers the cohomology of the associated regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties. We identify the Hessenberg functor with the microlocalization of Lusztig's character functor and compute the Hessenberg character using Lusztig's nonabelian Fourier pairing. More generally, for families of Hessenberg schemes defined by pure-dimensional $B$-stable closed cones in the tangent space $T_{eB}\mathcal B$, we show that monodromy on the intersection cohomology of regular semisimple fibers factors through $W$. When the cone is the tangent cone of a Schubert variety, we give a local condition at $eB$ under which the same character formula computes the graded $W$-character of this intersection cohomology. Combined with the methods of Precup and Sommers, our character formula can be used to compute the graded $W$-characters of all regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties in all Lie types of rank at most ten, including all exceptional types. These computations also motivate positivity and unimodality conjectures for Hessenberg varieties and Lusztig varieties in types $B$, $C$, and $D$, together with positivity conjectures for their partial flag versions.

papers.title: The distribution of small gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function
papers.summary: Let $0<γ_1\leq γ_2\leq \cdots$ be the ordinates of the non-trivial zeros $ρ_n$ of the Riemann zeta function in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity. Selberg proved unconditionally that there exists $λ_0<1$ such that a positive proportion of the zeros $ρ_n$ satisfy $γ_{n+1}-γ_n\leq 2πλ_0/\log γ_n$. Simonič, Trudgian and Turnage-Butterbaugh were the first to obtain an explicit value in Selberg's theorem, showing that $λ_0=1- 10^{-3\cdot 10^{13}}$ is admissible. This was considerably improved by Zhao who showed that $λ_0= 1-2.36\cdot 10^{-6}$ is admissible. In this paper, we use a different approach, based on an unconditional variant of Montgomery's pair correlation method, to obtain a substantial improvement of these results, showing unconditionally that $λ_0=0.7892<4/5$ is admissible.

papers.title: Smooth weak log Fano orbifolds are Campana rationally connected
papers.summary: Let \(X\) be a smooth projective complex variety with a boundary divisor \(Δ=\sum_{i=1}^s(1-1/m_i)D_i\) of simple normal crossings support and integers $m_i$. We prove that, if \(-(K_X+Δ)\) is nef and big, then \((X,Δ)\) is Campana rationally connected. We do this by constructing a free Campana rational curve whose class lies in the interior of the nef cone of curve classes and whose contacts with \(D_i\) have order \(m_i\) and avoid deeper strata. We construct such a curve from a free Campana curve by attaching to it free rational curves which intersect positively with divisors that span the cone of effective divisors, and smooth the resulting comb.

papers.title: Higher Noncommutative Motives and Higher K-theory
papers.summary: We construct higher additive noncommutative motives of stable $(\infty,n)$-categories, extending the additive motives of Blumberg, Gepner, and Tabuada and the secondary theory of Mazel-Gee and Stern. We formulate a notion of exact sequences and establish the universal property of the resulting additive motives. We give two equivalent constructions: a localization of enriched presheaves and a weighted Waldhausen $S$-construction on complete exact flags. We then compute their Hom objects, obtaining ordinary K-theory at the first level and lower additive motives recursively at higher levels. Our results recover the classical and secondary theories, provide coherent multiplicative structures, and yield an endofunctor on the category of Stefanich rings. In short, higher motives are higher K-theory.

papers.title: On the topology of some linear systems of hyperelliptic curves in Hirzebruch surfaces
papers.summary: Following a program suggested by Dolgachev and Libgober in 1981, we study the topology of the locus of smooth sections of linear systems of hyperelliptic curves on Hirzebruch surfaces. Within this class of examples, we find that a variety of behaviors occur - in some situations the enriched monodromy faithfully captures the fundamental group, and in others it does not. Our arguments mainly leverage algebro-geometric techniques to compute cohomological obstructions to families of embeddings.

papers.title: Stability Conditions on Twisted Derived Categories I: Existence and Full Numerical Support
papers.summary: We prove that for every nonempty smooth projective variety $X$ over an arbitrary field and every Brauer class $α$, the twisted derived category $D^b(X,α)$ admits a Bridgeland stability condition with full numerical support. papers.title: A complete classification of permutation binomials of the form $X^r(X^{2(q-1)}+a)$ over finite fields
papers.summary: Let $q$ be a prime power. We determine, for all positive integers $e$ and $r$, the coefficients $a\in\mathbb{F}_{q^e}$ for which $X^r(X^{2(q-1)}+a)$ permutes $\mathbb{F}_{q^e}$. For odd $q$ and $a\ne0$ there are no such permutations when $e\geqslant4$ is even. Over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$, with $r$ unrestricted, the permutation binomials are characterized by congruence and coprimality conditions on $r$ and equations of degree at most two for $(-a)^{(q+1)/2}$, together with one sporadic family over $\mathbb{F}_{11^2}$; this gives an explicit form of Hou's finiteness theorem for each fixed odd $r>3$. The remaining cases follow from the known classification for the exponent difference $q-1$. In the quadratic case, power sums whose binomial expansions are sparse by Lucas' theorem determine the exponent one $p$-adic digit at a time. In even degree at least four, an exponent congruence reduces the problem to the existence of a collision, which we obtain by counting norm ratios on the projective line. A power substitution extends the classification to $X^r(X^{d(q-1)}+a)$ whenever $\gcd\bigl(d,(q^e-1)/(q-1)\bigr)=2$.

papers.title: Gromov-Witten Nonvanishing and Symplectic Deformations of Toric Varieties
papers.summary: Let $A$ be nonzero in the cohomology ring of a smooth projective toric variety $X$. In this note, we observe the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A, A, \ldots\rangle_{0, n,β}^X$ as a consequence of Iritani's work on the big quantum cohomology ring of $X$. This implies Kollár's conjecture on the symplectic deformation invariance of rational connectedness in the case where $X$ is toric. If $X$ is moreover Fano and $B$ is also nonzero in the cohomology ring, we prove the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A,B,*\rangle_{0,3,β}^X$ using Batyrev's presentation of the small quantum cohomology ring of $X$. We conclude with a few consequences of this nonvanishing result.

papers.title: Heavy-Light Wall Crossings and Motivic Asymptotics of Moduli Spaces of Curves. Part I: Stabilization Graphs and Euler Characteristics
papers.summary: In this paper, we develop an explicit calculation of ordinary topological Euler characteristics of the coarse moduli spaces underlying Hassett spaces in the minimal all-light chamber and the Deligne-Mumford compactification. For genus $g\ge2$, we organize the calculation through a decomposition indexed by stabilization graphs and their decorations. The Burnside-Lefschetz formula allows us to compute the resulting contributions, taking into account graph symmetries and their fixed loci. The calculation in genus two illustrates the method explicitly and, in the Deligne-Mumford case, recovers the generating function of G. Bini, G. Gaiffi, and M. Polito (arXiv:math/9806048), with the corrections of G. Bini and J. Harer (arXiv:math/0506083), providing a check on the construction. We also carry out the calculation in genus three in an appendix. Together with an elementary genus-one calculation based on collision partitions and rational necklaces, these formulas yield complete asymptotic expansions as the number of labeled markings tends to infinity. The passage from all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics is governed by the universal change of variables $Φ(z)=(2-z)e^z-2$, which we derive by a direct wall-crossing argument. For arbitrary fixed genus $g\ge2$, the same framework identifies the leading contribution of rational trivalent graphs and gives the ordinary asymptotic scale $n!(e-2)^{-n}n^{(3g-5)/2}$. The leading constants are the symmetry weights of these graphs; we derive their generating function, recurrence, and large-genus behavior. We also determine the asymptotic ratio of all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics, answering a question of S. Kannan, S. Serpente, and C. H. Yun (arXiv:2207.02800).

papers.title: Birational Geometry of K-Moduli Spaces of Genus Four Curves
papers.summary: We study the wall-crossings for K-moduli spaces of (3,3)-curves on $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$. Together with the boundary polarized Calabi--Yau moduli space, these spaces interpolate between the GIT moduli space of (3,3)-curves and the Baily--Borel compactification of the moduli space of K3 surfaces arising as cyclic triple covers of $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$ branched along such curves. As applications, we describe the corresponding birational models in the Hassett--Keel--Looijenga program and realize the K-moduli space of degree one del Pezzo surfaces through explicit wall-crossings.

papers.title: Cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution from finite Prym data
papers.summary: We study how many polarized anti-invariant factors of the intermediate Jacobians of smooth Eckardt hyperplane sections determine a cubic fourfold with a symplectic involution. In rank three, the equation is determined by its fixed cubic surface and a conic in the dual projective space. The Torelli theorem of Casalaina-Martin--Zhang recovers the surface together with one plane section from each factor. When the surface has no automorphisms, these planes can be compared in a common dual space, and reconstruction reduces to classical conic interpolation. Five factors suffice without parameter data, and four suffice with their ordered parameter configuration; both bounds are sharp. In rank two, we construct two-dimensional families of pairwise nonisomorphic equivariant fourfolds with the same entire unparametrized Prym image. For a fixed fourfold, we also show that the closure of the anti-invariant factor family in an associated OG10 compactification is an integral projective Lagrangian subvariety.

papers.title: The residual map as a stratified fibration over the resonance arrangement
papers.summary: Given a stratum $\mathcal{H}(μ)$ of meromorphic one-forms on a Riemann surface with prescribed orders of zeros and poles, the residual map assigns to each differential the collection of its residues at the poles. In this paper, we prove that the residual map is a locally trivial topological fibration over each open flat of the stratification induced by the resonance arrangement. To give an algebro-geometric proof of this result, we introduce a refined compactification of the projectivized stratum $\mathbb{P}\mathcal{H}(μ)$, namely the moduli space of residue-aligned multi-scale differentials $\operatorname{RAMS}(μ)$. We prove that the projectivized residual map extends to $\operatorname{RAMS}(μ)$ as a stratified fibration over the projectivized resonance arrangement, thereby yielding a resolution of the projectivized residual map. This approach naturally extends to the analogue of the residual map for strata of $k$-differentials. Complementing the algebro-geometric approach, we also develop a flat-geometric point of view. In genus zero, each isoresidual fiber carries a canonical higher-dimensional analogue of a translation structure. These fibers admit a metric completion whose boundary has a modular interpretation in terms of the WYSIWYG compactification, for which we provide explicit local models. Isoresidual fibers admit a polyhedral cell decomposition whose geometry varies linearly with the underlying configuration of residues in period coordinates. Degenerations of these cells occur precisely when resonance conditions are satisfied, providing a geometric proof that the residual map is a stratified fibration. Finally, certain isoresidual fibers admit natural interpretations as Hurwitz spaces of branched covers, yielding unexpected homeomorphisms between moduli spaces of covers with prescribed ramification profiles.

papers.title: A sharp bound for the $a$-number of a cyclic cover of $\mathbb{P}^1$
papers.summary: Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. We give upper bounds for the $a$-number $a(X)$ when $X$ is hyperelliptic or, more generally, a tame cyclic cover of the projective line. For hyperelliptic curves, writing $g=pm+r$ with $0\le r<p$ and $n=(p-1)/2$, we prove the sharp bound $a(X)\le nm+\min\{n,r\}$. For tame cyclic covers, we refine previously known upper bounds and give curves attaining the resulting bound in infinitely many genera in characteristics $3$ and $5$. The proofs combine an alternating pairing on the bundle of locally exact differentials, originally due to Raynaud, with an explicit polynomial description of the Cartier operator. We also produce an explicit locus of hyperelliptic curves $X$ with $a(X)\ge a_g$, where $\frac{a_g}{g}$ converges to $\frac{p-1}{2p}$ as $g$ goes to $\infty$, whose dimension grows linearly with the genus $g$. These families exhibit excess intersections of the Torelli locus with loci of large $a$-number in the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties.

papers.title: Cluster-theoretic Newton--Okounkov polytopes of flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$
papers.summary: Newton--Okounkov bodies have been used for studying toric degenerations of flag varieties. We classify the Newton--Okounkov polytopes associated with cluster valuations and the anticanonical line bundle on full flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$. In type $A_4$, the $672$ seeds of cluster type $D_6$ yield $162$ affine unimodular equivalence classes, which coincide with the combinatorial equivalence classes. We determine the subgroup of exchange-graph automorphisms preserving every polytope class. It is a Klein four group of index six in the automorphism group of the exchange graph of cluster type $D_6$. In type $B_2$, we give defining inequalities for all six seeds. At the anticanonical weight, the two combinatorial equivalence classes split into three affine unimodular equivalence classes. Their respective class-preserving automorphism groups have orders four and two.

papers.title: New $\mathrm{C}_2$-equivariant infinite families and the $\mathrm{H}\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$-Hurewicz image
papers.summary: Let $a$ denote the stabilization of the Euler class of the sign representation of $\mathrm{C}_2$. In this paper, we show that the Behrens-Shah periodic $u$-self-equivalence of $C(a^i)$ -- a direct consequence of J.F. papers.title: Centres and semisimple deformations of contraction algebras
papers.summary: Let $A_{\rm{con}}$ be the contraction algebra of a $3$-fold flop of an irreducible curve, with genus-zero Gopakumar-Vafa invariants $n_1, \dots, n_l$. We show that $\prod_j M_j(\mathbb{C})^{n_j}$ is the only semisimple algebra to which $A_{\rm{con}}$ deforms. Hence $A_{\rm{con}}$ encodes its Gopakumar-Vafa invariants intrinsically, answering a question of Wemyss. Hua and Toda showed that this deformation exists, and Jelisiejew and Smoktunowicz proved its uniqueness in types A and D. The key step in our proof is that the centre of $A_{\rm{con}}$ has dimension $n_1 + \dots + n_l$. To prove this, we lift the contraction algebra of the universal flop to the Cartan subalgebra, where it becomes a corner of a deformed preprojective algebra. We show that the universal contraction algebra and its zeroth Hochschild homology are free over a polynomial ring, with presentations whose determinants are products of roots. Pulling these presentations back along the arc that classifies the flop gives the count, and recovers Toda's formula for $\dim A_{\rm{con}}$. We also prove Hua and Toda's flatness conjecture, and determine which Gopakumar-Vafa invariants occur in lengths 3 to 6.

papers.title: Arithmetic Kac Theory for Ramified Species
papers.summary: Let $K=k((t))$, where $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, and let $Λ$ be an acyclic ramified species over $K$. An indecomposable $Λ$-module can split after extending $K$. The number of its distinct geometric indecomposable summands is the degree of its residue endomorphism field $\operatorname{End}_Λ(M)/\operatorname{rad}\operatorname{End}_Λ(M)$. We use the positive roots and cyclic automorphism of the unfolded quiver to determine the number of isomorphism classes at every nonzero rank and residue degree $e\ge1$: it is zero, an explicitly computable finite number, or $|K|$. For every invariant imaginary root of the unfolding, including at nonprimitive ranks, we construct a smooth invariant family of absolutely indecomposable representations whose rational quotient by the change-of-bases group has dimension $1-q_d(β)$. We characterize ranks admitting absolutely Schur representations by the Schur roots of the unfolded quiver. For the associated species over finite fields, we realize the polynomials counting absolutely indecomposable representations as graded traces of the unfolding automorphism on preprojective BPS cohomology. Galois-orbit formulas and Möbius inversion then recover the counts at each residue degree. Finally, we prove an all-rank symmetrizable analogue of Kac's constant-term conjecture: the constant term of the polynomial counting all indecomposables, rather than only absolutely indecomposable ones, equals the corresponding Kac--Moody root multiplicity. This constant is independent of the symmetrizer and modulation.

papers.title: Functors from Lagrangian correspondences for wrapped sheaf categories
papers.summary: We consider the category of sheaves on a manifold with microsupport in a singular conic Lagrangian, and more generally microsheaves on the Lagrangian skeleton of a Weinstein manifold with stop, which are equivalent to ind-completions of partially wrapped Fukaya categories. Compact objects in these categories are obtained as wrappings of constructible sheaves with perfect stalks; they correspond to objects built from exact Lagrangians in finitely many steps. We give a microlocal criterion on constructible (micro)sheaves with perfect (micro)stalks which guarantees that the corresponding wrapped sheaves induce integral kernels that preserve compact objects of these categories. This generalizes a result of Gao on Lagrangian correspondences between fully wrapped Fukaya categories.

papers.title: Simple algebraic groups with good reduction, the genus problem, and unramified cohomology
papers.summary: We obtain a number of new results on the arithmetic of linear algebraic groups over higher-dimensional fields. In particular, we resolve some key open questions over 2-dimensional global fields, such as the finiteness of the genus of spinor groups of quadratic forms of dimension $\geq 10$. We also extend various finiteness results to new classes of fields, including function fields of $p$-adic surfaces. Our arguments rely in a crucial way on new finiteness results for unramified cohomology.

papers.title: Diophantine definability from addition and divisibility over rings of $S$-integers
papers.summary: Let $K$ be a number field, let $S$ be a finite set of places of $K$ containing the archimedean places, and let $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ denote the ring of $S$-integers of $K$. We prove that multiplication is positive-existentially definable in $(\mathcal{O}_{K,S},0,1,+,\mid)$ if and only if the unit group $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}^\times$ is infinite. This extends a 1977 theorem of Lipshitz for rings of integers to rings of $S$-integers. One of the key ingredients is a uniform bound for unit equations due to Evertse, Schlickewei and Schmidt, which we use to recover multiplication on the unit group.

papers.title: Global Green-Schwarz response on quaternionic sphere bundles
papers.summary: Local anomaly polynomials describe local variations, but a normalized Green-Schwarz phase also depends on global background data. We explain this dependence for ten-dimensional three-sphere bundles of quaternionic lines over closed spin seven-manifolds. The backgrounds retain two specified $\mathrm{Spin}(16)$ gauge bundles and an integral differential trivialization on the base, including its boundary identifications. The trivialized class is the sum of half the first Pontryagin class of the tangent bundle and the second Chern class of the quaternionic line's underlying complex bundle. For these backgrounds, the calculation combines a generally nonzero local Green-Schwarz integral with a real eta invariant evaluated by a twelve-dimensional Atiyah-Patodi-Singer filling. Together, these terms determine an integral relative characteristic number; the additive response is one third of that number, modulo integers. When the base's third and fourth rational cohomology groups vanish, the response equals eight times the Crowley-Goette invariant, without assuming that the base is simply connected. A calibration using the actual quaternionic line bundle gives additive value one third on $\mathrm{Sp}(2)$, recovering the known third-root phase. Distinct integral String data on one fixed ten-manifold give all three phase values, showing which global background information the response can detect. The physical identifications retain their prescribed fermion data, while the separate application to integral topological modular forms and vertex operator superalgebras requires compatible integral lifts. The response calculation constructs neither a microscopic realization nor an equivalence of complete theories.

papers.title: When do all iterates of $x^2 + a$ have maximal Galois group?
papers.summary: We provide an (in our opinion) simpler proof of the main results of [Stoll1992,Li2020,Li2021] on the question for which integers $a$ the Galois groups of all iterates of $x^2 + a$ are maximal (equivalently, the associated arboreal Galois representation is surjective). At the same time, we extend the results to rational parameters $a$. The main result states that for a subset of rational numbers of relative density $1/2$ in the complement of a certain open interval, the maximality of the Galois group of the second iterate is sufficient for the arboreal Galois representation to be surjective. We also discuss experimental evidence suggesting that a similar statement involving the fourth iterate may hold in general. The results were obtained in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic's AI model); they are also formalized in Lean (except for the experimental evidence).

papers.title: Trivial solutions in Generalized Fermat equations
papers.summary: The modular method is a powerful tool to study generalized Fermat equations. Trivial solutions often become an obstruction to the method. While using hypergeometric motives to construct Galois representations, some of these solutions give rise to newforms with complex multiplication. In the present article, assuming a standard conjecture in Darmon's program, we prove that asymptotically any newform with complex multiplication cannot be related to a non-trivial primitive solution. This allows to discard all such newforms, including those associated to trivial solutions.

papers.title: Magnitude, path and coarse homology
papers.summary: In this article, we introduce Borel--Moore and uniformly finite versions of magnitude homology and path homology for locally finite graphs by allowing possibly infinite chains subject to local finiteness and boundedness conditions. In both settings, we construct magnitude--path spectral sequences extending the spectral sequence studied by the author. Their E^1-pages are given by the corresponding magnitude homologies, their E^2-pages contain the corresponding path homologies on the p-axis, and they converge to coarse homology and uniformly finite homology, respectively, in the sense of Nowak--Yu. Moreover, the E^{r+1}-page is invariant under r- homotopy, whereas the homology to which the spectral sequence converges is invariant under coarse equivalence. Thus the spectral sequences interpolate between small-scale and large-scale geometry. We also show that the Borel--Moore and uniformly finite magnitude homologies are products and restricted products, respectively, of ordinary magnitude homology groups with a fixed initial point. Hence the E^1-page is assembled from pointwise magnitude-homological data, providing a mechanism for combining local information into global large-scale invariants. As applications, we establish Mayer--Vietoris sequences for magnitude homology, path homology, the associated spectral-sequence pages, and coarse and uniformly finite homology. We also show that diagonality of ordinary magnitude homology implies degeneration at the E^2-page, yielding isomorphisms between path homology and the corresponding coarse homology. Finally, we discuss applications to Cayley graphs of graph products, including right-angled Artin groups and right-angled Coxeter groups.

papers.title: Infinity operad pairs, higher distributivity and spectral Tambara functors
papers.summary: We introduce an $\infty$-categorical model of operad pairs and their associated bimonoidal categories. We study the related concepts such as cocartesian-cartesian operad pairs, algebra pairs and the Day convolution. Using the Day convolution for operad pairs, we can define distributive functors between a symmetric bimonoidal category and a cartesian closed monoidal category. As an application, we show that for a finite group $G$, the operadic distributive functors from $\mathrm{Span}(\mathsf{Fin}_G)$ to any cartesian closed monoidal category coincides with the distributive functors defined by the distributive diagram. Therefore, we show that the connective $G$-equivariant $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectra are equivalently the spectral $G$-Tambara functors.

papers.title: Orbit Transversality for Projective Space
papers.summary: Let $f\colon \mathbb{P}^n\to \mathbb{P}^n$ be a dominant endomorphism defined over a number field $K$. We show that there is a finite extension $L/K$ such that every proper closed subset of $\mathbb{P}^n$ misses at least one grand $(f,L)$-orbit. Equivalently, $(\mathbb{P}^n,f,K)$ is strongly dense orbit transversal (S-DOT): every set containing exactly one representative of each grand $(f,L)$-orbit is Zariski dense in $\mathbb{P}^n$.

papers.title: The $\mathbb Q$-gonality of $X_1(42)$ is $12$
papers.summary: We prove that the $\mathbb F_5$-gonality and the $\mathbb Q$-gonality of the modular curve $X_1(42)$ are both $12$, improving the previous lower bound of $10$. Since $J_1(42)(\mathbb Q)$ is finite, it follows that $12$ is the least degree in which $X_1(42)$ has infinitely many points. The lower bound comes from an exhaustive search over Riemann--Roch spaces, following Derickx and van Hoeij, using a new reduction by the orbits of a cyclic group of automorphisms of order $12$ on places of degree at most $5$ ($743\,231$ Riemann--Roch spaces). An earlier search with the reductions from van Hoeij's code (about $3$ million Riemann--Roch spaces, about $6$ times more CPU time) gives the same result and serves as supporting evidence. We prove the reductions and record the data needed to reproduce the computations.

papers.title: Permutation polynomials from quadratic and linear forms
papers.summary: We investigate a family of permutation polynomials of finite fields using the theory of quadratic and linear forms. In this paper, we begin with a general treatment over arbitrary fields of characteristic not $2$, and then provide explicit characterizations for several classes of such permutation polynomials.

papers.title: Koszul duality and homotopy algebras for operads over quivers
papers.summary: For a quiver $Q$, we introduce and study $Q$-operads (or operads over $Q$), defined as a special sort of $\mathbf{fc}$-multicategories or virtual double categories, in which the directions of the arrows of $Q$ encode the permitted input orderings. In this higher operadic framework, we construct the bar--cobar adjunction and develop a theory of Koszul duality and homotopy algebras, together with compatibility results under changes of quiver. We treat dg categories and their left modules, right modules, and bimodules as algebras over quiver-operads. We prove that these operads are Koszul and that their resolutions govern the corresponding $A_\infty$ categories and modules. We also categorify Sagave's notion of derived $A_\infty$ algebras and introduce modules over derived $A_\infty$ algebras and categories. Finally, we explain that restriction along a folding of quivers constructs diagonal $A_\infty$ bimodules, while extension along an inclusion of quivers realizes two-sided bar models of derived tensor products.

papers.title: Categorical Torelli and Fourier-Mukai partners of hypersurfaces
papers.summary: Let $X\subset\PP^{M-1}$ be a smooth hypersurface of degree $d<M$, and let $\Ku(X)$ be its Kuznetsov component, the orthogonal complement of the line bundles $\OO_X,\dots,\OO_X(M-d-1)$ in the derived category. We prove that $\Ku(X)$ determines $X$ for every smooth quartic in $\PP^{4k+1}$, $k\geq1$; together with earlier work, this gives categorical Torelli for every smooth hypersurface of degree $d<M$ with $d\nmid M$. The same algebraic reconstruction proves the classical generic Torelli theorem for these quartics, which completes generic Torelli for smooth hypersurfaces whose degree does not divide $M$, cubic surfaces excepted. When $d$ divides $M$, the Kuznetsov component is a Calabi--Yau category, as for cubic fourfolds, where categorical Torelli is known to fail. We show that, apart from cubic fourfolds, such a hypersurface has a number of Fourier--Mukai partners bounded by a constant depending only on $d$ and $M$, and that categorical Torelli holds in sufficiently large degree, in every dimension. The main tool is a deformation theorem: when geometric deformations surject onto the second Hochschild cohomology of the Kuznetsov components, an equivalence deforms together with the hypersurfaces, so statements proved for general hypersurfaces extend to all smooth ones.

papers.title: Density and holes of the visible points in certain cut-and-project sets
papers.summary: We study the set of visible points from the origin in certain cut-and-project sets, specifically the density of the set. We generalize to all real quadratic number fields the formulas for the density found by G. Hammarhjelm, and the corresponding error bounds proved by I. Gringlaz, R. Kumar, B. Weiss. We also find the possible densities of the set of visible points in the cut-and-project set, with a constant generic lattice, and a changing window with constant volume. We also study bounds for the distance of large holes in the set of visible points of certain cut-and-project sets, generalizing theorems originally proved by P. Erdős for $\mathbb{Z}^2$.

papers.title: On the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties of the differential system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$
papers.summary: A prolongation variety of a polynomial differential system $S$ is an algebraic variety defined by the equations of $S$ and their derivatives up to a given order. We compute the geometric degree of the prolongation varieties associated with the system $x_1'=x_2^2$, $x_2'=x_1^2$ in terms of the prolongation order, thereby proving a conjecture stated by Gleb Pogudin in Section 2, Question 6 of "Some Open Problems in Differential Algebra". Our approach is motivated from the beginning by doing computational experiments in OSCAR in order to find the number of solutions of a zero-dimensional system using algebraic Thomas decomposition. The result will follow from a coprimality condition on a family of polynomials with integer coefficients, which is verified by showing that their roots satisfy a strong interlacing property. Finally, we propose an extension of the conjecture for the systems $x_1'=x_2^n$, $x_2'=x_1^n$ with $n>2$.

papers.summary: Let $p\ge5$ be a prime number, $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. papers.title: On Rankin Invariants of Ideal Lattices
papers.summary: The Rankin constant $γ_{n,k}$ measures the largest discriminant of a densest rank $k$ sublattice of a lattice in $\R^n$ over all such lattices of rank $n$ and their exact values are mostly open. For a general lattice $L\subset \R^n$ of rank $n$, the problem of determining its Rankin invariant $γ_{n,k}(L)$ is to find the discriminant of such a densest sublattice. There are no general formulas to compute the discriminant of any arbitrary rank $k$ sublattice. This paper specializes to the case of ideal lattices arising from ideals of number fields, and provides two approaches to study Rankin constants: first, we propose a systematic approach to approximate the minimum discriminant by introducing subideal lattices and proving a closed-form formula to compute $γ^{ideal}_{n,k}(L)$, the ideal Rankin invariant of the ideal lattice. Subsequently, we establish necessary conditions on the underlying number field for the existence of an ideal lattice admitting an optimal subideal lattice with a prescribed minimum discriminant. Secondly, we consider ideal lattices with arbitrary sublattices. We compute $γ_{9,2}$ and improve the current known bounds of the Rankin constants $γ_{5,2}$, $γ_{7,2}$ and $γ_{9,3},γ_{9,4}$, and provide an algebraic construction of the lattice that was used in dimensions $5$ and $7$.

This paper specializes to the case of ideal lattices arising from ideals of number fields, and provides two approaches to study Rankin constants: first, we propose a systematic approach to approximate the minimum discriminant by introducing subideal lattices and proving a closed-form formula to compute $\gamma^{ideal}_{n,k}(L)$, the ideal Rankin invariant of the ideal lattice. Subsequently, we establish necessary conditions on the underlying number field for the existence of an ideal lattice admitting an optimal subideal lattice with a prescribed minimum discriminant. Secondly, we consider ideal lattices with arbitrary sublattices. We compute $\gamma_{9,2}$ and improve the current known bounds of the Rankin constants $\gamma_{5,2}$, $\gamma_{7,2}$ and $\gamma_{9,3},\gamma_{9,4}$, and provide an algebraic construction of the lattice that was used in dimensions $5$ and $7$.
